text: This is definitely my favorite in and out restaurant. Your chicken is very tender and cooked all the way, and the service is pretty good. Their sauces are to die for too!

I MISS CHIHUAHUA'S!!!  The wonderful authentic flavor of the food, and the neighborhood feel of the old restaurant was so much better.  New Casa Juarez just doesn't even come close to comparing with the old restaurant. I've been twice now... once for lunch, and once for dinner. Both times the salsa was bland, the food was barely mediocre, and the service was sooooo slow. The only good thing I have to say as that the new menu's are very nice. The ones at Chihuahuas were getting a little shabby. 

I will probably try it 1 more time of they're still around in a year.

Unfortunately, the last few times I've been to Nicky's, I've left very underwhelmed. I've probably been about five times? And nothing has ever lived up to that first experience. 

On the current menu, several dishes kind of missed the mark for me a bit: the spinach and ricotta ravioli was a little flat, the crab fusili was too much cheese and butter and I missed the lemon and crab, the rabbit campanelle was okay but didn't wow us. I like their white pizzas but often find their red sauce to be too watery and needing a little seasoning. 

I will likely keep trying Nicky's every once in a while, because I like it despite the misses, I like its location (not in the Gulch, East Nashville, Downtown, Germantown), and I just love and crave Italian food and pasta. But I think Nicky's is suffering from what A LOT of restaurants in Nashville suffer from - inconsistency. You'll eat something you LOVE and go back hoping to have a similar experience to leave slightly disappointed. I'm waiting for Nicky's to hit their stride again! I'm optimistic.

text:
I don't understand all the hype that surrounds El Charro.  Yes, it's very old, but the way they expended and opened all the new locations takes away from the excitement.

It's OK though.  The food seems like it's prepared nicely and the service is usually good.  I just think there are better places in Tucson.

Wow! Sooooooooooo good!
We stopped in without a reservation on a Saturday night and we were able to be seated within a minute or so. The hostess was very accommodating and the waitress was super friendly. The food was AMAZING. The butternut squash ravioli was phenomenal! The dessert selection was delicious. I will definitely be back!

SO SO delicious!! What a gem to have so close to our house!. I love that this is within walking distance. They do a lot of take out business. We got their menu in the mail and it said dine in and get a free margarita, it was on the rock, original style (my favorite) and had tequila in it! Pitchers are only $6 and we'll be doing that next time definitely. It's BYOB, so the pitcher does not contain alcohol because they can't sell alcohol. I go the burrito with mole. The mole is heavenly. I hear they make it right there! The burrito was bigger than my face and it had plenty of cheese, but not like Chi-Chi's where everything was layered in cheese. These tastes were perfectly tuned. The restaurant has such wonderful bright colors; it's so cheerful! I can't wait to go back. Highly recommend Buena Vista. (Even the "not-recommended" Yelp reviews love this restaurant!!)

I wanted to give this more stars when I first came in but with no a/c it's hard to do.  Today probably cost another star since they haven't had A/C for the past 3 days.  It's been grueling to wait extra time due to staff shortages and to try to sit and eat in humidity while you sweat.  
We came at 11am for I'm pretty sure they won't stay open too long so long as the days keep reaching 90 degrees.  They also don't have enough condiments like ketchup, hot sauce, or syrup aside form the 2 bottles of each shared between 15 tables or so.  
Service from the kitchen or the communication from the server to the kitchen has a variety of problems from food items missing, cook instructions not followed, cold food, and not enough wait staff to handle this place when tables are full.  I have the best tip that will improve the visit for us it's asking for Carol, she really does work hard to check on you and fix any problems.  She is running all over the place trying to get to each table.  
Probably best to come during off hours when 1 server might only have 1-4 tables, if you don't have a lot of time or patient or don't want to sweat lol and maybe stay away from weekends or brunch hours.

Cochon isn't normally open on Sundays so we definitely lucked out. We arrived with a reservation but still had to wait as it was very crowded. 

I was with a great group of girls who were adventurous and willing to try anything.

Rabbit and dumplings, Lousiana Cochon with cracklings, Short ribs, Roasted oysters, Gumbo, Hot buttery rolls, & Shrimp. For Dessert, we shared Port, Apple pie and Butterscotch pudding.

Every dish was expertly prepared and we polished off everything down to the last bite. We tried not to fill up on the bread but ended up using it to sop up the sauces and gravies.

The table next to us got the special which was basically a whole fried pig. The 5 of them tackled it like a pro! It looked so good, especially the crispy skin. I had to resist the urge to lean over and stick my fork in for a bite. 

Bravo, Cochon! I would absolutely recommend this place to anyone in NOLA looking for a trendy spot with great food and an interesting mix of cocktails.

Fantastic German food!  Based on the Yelp reviews we called ahead for a Monday evening (Memorial day) reservation.  We thought we'd need it, but we arrived and only 5 other tables were taken (about 3/4 of the place was empty).  

We were quickly greeted by Veronica (the proprietor) in German.  She seems like a great ball of energy!  Jonathan quickly brought out our drinks (Optimator on tap = 1 star on its own!)

We ordered, but didn't want to over-order....Veronica made us something special.  We had the:
-Spazle with cheese (probably the best I've ever had)
-Wurzfleish - essentially a ramekin filled with pork and sauce that you eat with toast.  Veronica came out and prepared it for us the way "real Germans" eat it.  It was fabulous!
-A 1/2&1/2 Bratwurst, Bockwurst - seriously delicious
-Zigeuner Schnitzel - pounded pork, breaded, fried, and served with a red & green pepper sauce.

we were so full it hurt AND we took our food home.  Everything was delicious, our host was extremely welcoming, and the experience was great.  I wish we could have been there on a more lively night to get a real feel for the hospitality (and joviality) that must happen at this restaurant.

Go here, you won't be disappointed.  In fact, we passed a bunch of restaurants on the main drag (State) on our way to this place....everyone in them looked depressed.  They should have gone to Brummis!

First this is a beautiful place! It's to bad no one who works there seems to care. From the 3 young ladies at the hostess station who were to busy talking to bother with us, so we seated ourselves at the bar. The bartender once again was busy talking, at the far end of the bar to a. Customer and a waiter. We finally got menus and ordered when the order arrived it had just been sloppily plated, my husband also had asked for broccoli and no green beans so 15 minutes later we got the broccoli. My silverware was delivered dirty no apologies nothing! Really sad!! 
The food was just average, and the house made Thousand Island was mustard based? 
Strange

I felt like I'd gotten kicked in the gut when I got handed a 12 ounce cup of decent coffee out of a carafe and charged 4$. Maybe some coffee shops can charge $4 for a coffee, but this is not one of them.

Dear Mr. Miller,

As a long time customer, I wanted you and your wife to know how disappointed I was this morning when I found out from an employee in the meat department when I placed my prime rib roast order that Jerry, your meat manager, was "long gone." I saw Jerry last Sunday working by himself. 

I have no idea why Jerry is no longer with your company, but in terms of customer service (the most important attribute in my book), Jerry was an asset to your company in a significant department in your store. Jerry provided outstanding customer service. It was obvious that he knew what he was doing in the meat department. I have spoken to Jerry weekly during my weekly Sunday shopping visits for years. I could always count on Jerry's friendliness (never rude), meat knowledge (and not just selling a product), and his trimming skills. He made your meat products shine despite a lack of other personnel in the meat department (on Sundays, always a busy shopping day). Jerry definitely kept your company going in the meat department. Jerry's departure is your company's loss. Good luck. I will give Jerry's replacement a chance to shine, like your store's physical plant. Your company has spent a lot of money upgrading your store. I hope you value your good employees too. If I stop seeing other familiar faces, then I will draw my one conclusions.

I am giving your company a five (5) star rating today, but I am still bothered by Jerry's absence nearly eight (8) hours after today's visit. I am sure I am not the only customer who will miss Jerry. It is my hope that Jerry's replacement is better than Jerry. If not, then my next rating will not be a five (5) star rating or worst yet, I will buy meat for my family elsewhere.

I know a little bit about good business. I am a local self-employed lawyer who depends on happy customers. Repeat business is something that every profitable business needs.

Mark J. Connor, Esquire

A friend told me there was a Skyline Chili in Florida and I said, "Where?". So it was then that I decided ROAD TRIP. Drive two and a half hours for a hotdog and some chili over spaghetti? Yep, this stuff is that good and it is inexpensive and it is addictive. This is Cincinnati Chili in the finest of Cincinnati chili tradition. It is thin, runny, and has a unique flavor, but it is also really good. So I got the Coney Dog which is like a mini hotdog with chili, cheese and probably onions and mustard on it. And a small plate of the 5 way Chili (chili, spaghetti, cheese, beans, and onions). If you are lucky ... really lucky they will have another Cincinnati tradition: Graeters ice cream, but don't get your hopes up because it sells out about as fast as they get it. If you get the chance, the flavor you want is Raspberry Chocolate. It is so cool this place is here, as it saves a long drive from Florida to Cincinnati. I mean, have you ever heard of a hot dog place that had table service, menu's and a server to bring stuff out? Well here you have. As a bonus, our server was really attentive and explained stuff to our friends who had never had this stuff before. It really is chili that is worth a five hour round trip road trip.

So excited to take my hubby today for lunch. Sorely diaappointed. Got a salad that was supposed to have 1/2 an avocado and found one small bite. Scant chicken that was dry, tough and had to put in my napkin. More romaine than anything. 14$ pricey for what was inside the bowl. Great idea, nice concept, would like to see it succeed because they are using locally grown veggies. But doubt we will go back. It did seem like there was no oversight with employees....too bad.

I've never heard of MOD before, but I'm a lover of all things pizza, so I decided to give this place a try with my co-workers. We were kindly greeted by the employees when we walked in and they asked if we had been there before. We said no, so they explained the whole process to us. It's simply a bar full of fresh fruits, vegetables, meats and cheeses, etc. and you are able to load your dough with as many toppings as you want all for one modest price (less than $8). They also have salads if you prefer a healthier option, but I'm all about the pizza. They also have a wall full of different combination choices if you don't know what to decide on. Those combinations are completely customizable as well. 

After we picked all of our toppings, our pizzas were placed in a fire breathing oven and we took our seats and waited for our name to be called. The wait is super fast, I'm pretty sure we waited no more then 4-5 minutes for our pizza. What I really like about their food is that everything on the pizza tastes fresh, from the crust to the toppings. It definitely makes you feel good about eating pizza. 

There's plenty of seating around the restaurant and there was an employee going around cleaning up the tables and chairs, which kept the restaurant looking very clean and presentable.

This review is not to be confused with my review on the Yelp Elite Event at Slapfish two weeks ago.  I came back today for lunch because their shrimp cocktail is that awesome.  I can't get over the sweet tangy cocktail sauce they call Rooster Cocktail Sauce.  I love the stuff!

Today I ordered the Power Bowl.  The mixed grilled seafood was shrimp, salmon and tilapia.  The vegetables were sliced carrots, petite tomatoes, cauliflower, broccoli, squash and sliced radishes.  Also included were plenty of sliced avocados, a hard boiled egg, some onions all on a bed of cabbage.  Hidden underneath the seafood was a generous portion of rice with a really unique sauce.

I thought about trying the Lobster Grinder so was able to sample the Spiced Aioli sauce.  I do love this sauce but this was a little bit too much of a kick for me.  Maybe next time I can get a substitute or the sauce withheld.

I came here while on Vacation with some friends. 
They were having a show that we wanted to see and being as I have a broken foot I was on crutches and wasn't too thrilled of going to a bar but we called ahead and they assured us that if we came an hour before the show we would be seated inside. 

We arrived at 5 for dinner (show started at 7) and were seated outside. I explained to the waiter that we had paid the $20 for the show that starts at 7 and he brought a manager around to our table who assured us that we be seated inside when a table became available. 

We ordered drinks and whoa it was not what we were expecting something really delicious as we ordered Hibiscus Cosmopolitans but it was more vodka with a bit of fresh lime it was basically like taking a vodka shot. I was not impressed.

Our waitress suggested that we get My Bee's Keeper since we were not thrilled with our drinks, and that was better but still not the best. 

Our waitress even said "Ya mixology is getting really crazy around here" if by crazy you mean not appealing then yes I agree. 

About an hour later we asked our waitress about going inside and she had no idea what we were talking about. The manager came by and apologized and said we would be going in soon. 

By 7pm the show started and we were still not seated. This time the manager was too busy to come by and speak to us so we ended up leaving at 7:30 when it became clear we were not going inside. 

The only reason why I'm giving them 2 stars is because the fries were really good and the only drink that was manageable was the House Old Fashioned. 

Will never come back

I definitely got off to the wrong foot, but . . . 

I've never had such overtly bad service. Certainly, I was inappropriate in stating that it seemed like people were "stressed" in the restaurant; but to tell me that I'm rude and that the best thing you [the server] can do is walk away - seems like extremely poor customer service. 

Actually, the conversation went like this - "Have things been busy tonight?"  Reply from bar tender,  "no, it's been terribly slow. Why?" My response, "it seems like people are a bit stressed." Reply from bar tender, "I can't interpret that as anything but rude, so I'm going to walk away." 

The bartender then proceeded to turn her back to me at the bar and talk about how "bad that guy is over there. He's driving me crazy." The conversation was loud enough that I could hear it 8 feet away.

To this, I placed $10 on the bar and left.  So, please understand that I'm not writing this review based on the food. My review is solely based on the poor service and a $10 club soda. As such, take this review for what you will; but I for one will never eat in Cochon. And, I've eaten at restaurants all over the world. The service was the absolute worst I have ever received. Anywhere.

As most of the other reviews state, the interior and over all design of the building interior and exterior is wonderful. Me and some of my co-workers decided to go here for our lunch break. Chips and salsa were fine, some a bit overcooked and burnt. 
No utensils or napkins until the actual food came out. Then my co-worker and I had the $15 shrimp culichi (which is crazy, I can go to Mariscos Chihuahua and get a larger portion for less) and the other had ceviche (a small is $12).
We were all enjoying our food until my co-worker was about to take a bite of her rice and took a double take because something was hanging out of it. We all paused and she said "Eww I'm about to throw up" as we look over there is a long blonde hair hanging out of her rice!!!
We called the waitress over and she makes the same face we all did. She walks away with the plate to come back two minutes later to ask if she wanted something else. Hesitantly, she orders a small ceviche (trying to stay as far away from some of that has rice as possible). 
If you've ever had any food with something other than what is supposed to be in your food, you are totally disgusted and have a ruined appetite. Because of that she had her ceviche in a to go cup with an empty stomach.
So, it comes time for us to pay and ask for our checks. And to our surprise she WAS CHARGED for her $15 culichi even though she had the hair in her rice and never ate it! When I asked for the manager the waitress serving the table next to us said they are not there and she can help. We explained the whole experience and she said she will be right back. Next, a waitress that was helping a family a couple tables down from us comes and says we will talk to the owner and let him know what happened, sorry. Leaving it at that she walked away, which I guess meant that was all they would do.

To say the least this was all our first and LAST time ever going to Casa full of hair Valencia! 
Customer service definitely isn't they're main priority, Bringing in the money is. Even if that means doing it the wrong way! I will be giving everyone my honest opinion which is to never go there!

Great Florida food, live music, affordable cocktails and good beer selection.  They also have kid's menu. Their key lime pie is delicious, and I haven't gotten sick from anything (we eat here about 2x per week).  They should serve Coke products though.  Only downside (and not sure if it's even legal) they have a smoking section right outside their front door.  It's the primo spot for sitting outside.  Per Florida regulations the smoking portion can't be more than 50% covered but this is.  It's also covered or screened on the sides.  They cater to smokers. Gross. Land o Lakes needs more dining options.

Horrible margarita.
Outside of that dinner was fine.
Usually only have lunch here, but stopped for dinner last night and it was ok.
Shrimp and oysters were fresh and very good.
BLackened prime rib was good, but a little fatty. Stuffed shrimp was also good.
I would have given this place another 1/2 except for one thing. Ordered a margarita which was the worst tasting thing in the world. We sent the margarita back and the waitress wanted to know exactly what was wrong. It was bad, didn't want it and ordered $40.00 of wine. When the bill comes the margarita was still on the bill. When I asked she said that she couldn't tell the bartender what was wrong with it so they left it on the charge. I will probably go back for lunch, but not real happy they didn't want to take the drink off the bill. It was $5.95 , so not the end of the world, but still, most GOOD restaurants will take off the any drink , or wine, that a patron doesn't like. 
Won't go for dinner again, since Vickers is close and has a wait staff that would have been more accomadating than the one we had.

We've been to this location several times already and each time we've come they've been fairly busy. Service is a hit or miss but we've always had a decent experience here. 

I ordered the curry katsu and was disappointed because my food came after my boyfriend's and was cold. I didn't realize it at first and took a couple more bites but in the end I had to let the server know and he was apologetic and offered to have another one made. To compensate for the food being cold they offered us deep fried squid, which was really nice of them. The squid was cooked just right and was nice and hot. Eventually another curry katsu was brought out and it was nothing spectacular but at least it was hot.

My boyfriend ordered the black garlic ramen and he enjoyed it. I guess when you go to a noodle bar, you really should be ordering noodles. That was my mistake this time and I'll probably order ramen the next time I eat there. 

Overall I would still pick Noodle bar by Nomiya over prairie noodle house (portions too small for the price) and Tokiwa (not flavourful enough) but I've only been to both of those places once and was not impressed with either of them.

Fiesta mexicana is located just off vista Blvd in the raleys shopping center.
Parking is a breeze with the restaurant sharing the huge lot with other businesses.
The restaurant itself has quite a few tables as well as booth seating.
We arrived around 10:30am on a Sunday, looking for a early lunch. Little did I know that they serve breakfast and open at 9am.
On Sundays, they have buy one Mimosa get one free.
There happy hour is daily from 3-6 pm and they offer buy one margarita get one free.
On Tuesday they have taco Tuesday, tacos are 99 cents with a choice of fillings.
I ordered a taco salad with chicken. It was delicious. It came inside a tortilla bowl. The bowl was filled with lettuce, beans, rice, guacamole, sour cream, salsa, tomato's and onions.
This was a meal in itself. I definitely will be back.

This place was top dog when it came to Italian Specialties before Carlino's came into play. It is family owned and run by John (owner) Gary (his son) and sometimes his wife will be slinging out lottery tickets, or helping out in the back. Nice lady, good family and they treat every customer in there like they were a part of their own. Right there you know customer service is something they believe in.

Their sandwich's are good in size, definitely better than Wawa, the freshness alone stands out there. It's a gonna be a good hoagie when you see and hear the hum of that slicer going. Slice after slice of those meats and cheeses in front of you, knowing it is there to soley satisfy your hunger. Not like other places that keep their meats and cheeses in a stainless steel dish, or a plastic dish. Those leave that taste of blah i guess, don't really know how to describe "blah " but I'm sure a facial expression explains "blah" better.  

I myself like to add roasted peppers , and long hots on any of their sandwich's.. just brings out the flavor even more. Now if you are a mayo fan, and want it on your sandwich , please don't do it. Adding mayo will  just bastardize the whole experience. 

   ***side note- I personally think the sandwich's could be bit bigger, more meat, pack it in there i say ***

In all you will be pleased with any of the fine selections, and you will be treated like family when you visit.

We went to Fork for the first time on my birthday for dinner and it was super delicious. I've lived in Old City for years and had always been curious. It's upscale but still a relatively casual atmosphere, with a variety of small dishes.

The tasting menu is very expensive, and honestly too much food for us, so we ordered a la carte and opted for a bottle of wine instead! We each ordered a small pasta, entrée, and shared a dessert. 

We started with the Saffron Fazzoletti with rabbit and the Potato Gnocchi. Both were amazing with so much flavor and my favorite part of the whole meal. For our mains we had the duck and cauliflower steak. Just a heads up the cauliflower steak is actually cauliflower prepared like steak, and was just incredible and the most filling thing I had.

It's very expensive, but it's a fun place for special occasions. I can't wait to try their famous brunch!

Sauce on the Side has been on my list ever since it opened however up until now it managed to never work out, however this past weekend the universe seemed to be in perfect alignment and I managed to be downtown around lunch and close by. 

As soon as I walked in the friendly staff greeted me with a warm welcome, and informed me of the days special. Now even thought I knew what I wanted they were friendly enough before my order to offer suggestions and even explain a few things. Now I have had time to review the menu and knew immediately that I wanted to try the Meet in St.Louie, which is a pretty basic pizza calzone minus the sauce, as it is served on the side a la their namesake.

The food here is amazing, but I am sure you already figured that out based on all the other reviews. I have had calzones at other places and the dough is always to much or tough, while at Sauce on the Side the dough is perfect, light and fluffy with a great taste. My meal, the Meet Me in St.Louie, was great. It is served with Pepperoni, Italian Sausage, Provel, Mascarpone, and Ricotta and bushed with garlic oil and served with a side of meat sauce. There is something magical about the way the Provel, Mascarpone, and Ricotta all blend together to great an amazing blend. Best Calzone Ever! 

I also had a chance to sample The Duke, and I can say that John Wayne would be proud of this calzone taking his namesake. The Duke is brushed with Smoked Chili Oil, and served with BBQ Pulled Chicken, Applewood Smoked Bacon, Corn Salsa, Smoked Cheddar, Mozzarella and a BBQ Ranch Sauce, it was amazing.  I seriously have a list of calzones to try here, I think the Figgy Piggy is next on my list.

Prices are reasonable for the portion size, seriously these are large calzones! This is a great place to grab a quick lunch or even a late dinner, they have a great casual atmoshpere here. SOTS also have a rather large beer selection for their size so go ahead and pick one from their 40+ beer list, best off all they are open late!

Overall Sauce on the Side is a great addition to downtown, and Saint Louis in general. These guys need to keep doing what they are doing because its great!

Overall Sauce on the Side is a great addition to downtown, and Saint Louis in general. These guys need to keep doing what they are doing because its great!

We had a party of 4 that luckily snagged reservations on their first night. I absolutely love the interior. It's gorgeous, modern, and left me feeling like I was in a NY or Vegas restaurant (the light fixtures..omg). Plus, I am SO glad they aren't doing the farm to table thing and there wasn't a flannel shirt in sight. Yes!

We had a very tough time deciding on what to order, but started small with the cocktail list. I had the honey and thyme with gin and it was absolutely delicious. The jimberly and southern belle were hits at the table as well. However, be prepared that they are $13.00 each, but also very well made. 

Our server was sure to tell us about the appetizers and sold us on what he called "an appetizer platter" (whatever you do, DON'T order this, but more later) which included short ribs, quail, octopus, and sausage. I also had to try the spicy lobster gnocchi. The appetizers were all good minus the octopus. No one liked it; it was cold and rubbery and we didn't even finish it all. But the quail...wow. Probably my favorite from the appetizers. 

They were out of the mushrooms and trout for the evening, so we all ended up ordering red meat; steak and the lamb osso bucco. All of them were great, but the sides were really outstanding. The crispy sweet potatoes I couldn't stop eating and I didn't even order them! But I can speak highly of the foie gras home fries with garlic mayo and grilled brussels were extremely good as well. All around a spectacular meal. 

With one big problem: 

Remember that appetizer platter that was sold to us at the beginning of the meal? They charged us for each individual item, and the sausage alone was $25. That's right. the cost of an entree. The grand total for our appetizer platter of 4 items (one of which we didn't eat) SEVENTY dollars. You read that correctly $70.00! OUCH. We felt completely duped. In fact, we didn't stop talking about it the rest of the evening. We talked to our waiter and he apologized but then made the fantastic comment: "We were told not to say the price." Baffled, we asked for the octopus to be taken off. He took them off without any push back, so that was nice, but we still were in shock about our bill. Ridiculous. 

So. Prima is great, but whatever you do, don't order the appetizer "platter" and make sure you know the price before ordering!

We had a reservation for 6:30 for 6. This is not an exaggeration.... we did not have our entrees until 8:30!!! This is my second time here, the first time was on Father's Day, the service then was insanely slow, but I figured it was because it was a busy holiday. Nope. Tonight wasn't that busy either! The owner came up to our table to inform us that she was short 2 cooks.... ok fine. But why not maybe to help him?!!! Seriously. Food is good don't get me wrong but really?!! 2 hours for entrees. Only reason we stayed is because my grandparents love the food and don't see to mind the wait tooo too much. It was at least 35 mins just to receive our drinks. Yeah the food is good, but keep in mind- make sure the rest of your day free

We went to Mitchell's Fish Market to celebrate my birthday this evening. Unfortunately, I am not sure we will return. While our food was delicious, the service was terrible. Our waiter didn't return to our table one single time after he delivered our drinks and took our order. Our wine/cocktails were empty when our entrees were delivered. Our waiter was nowhere in sight for a good 20 minutes. I understand wait staff needs a break (I am not sure if that's where he was), but no one assumed care of our table or even bothered to check in on us. Our appetizer and meals were brought out by the kitchen. No one offered anything else.  Given that we spent over $100 on two dinners, an app and two drinks, I had much higher expectations for service.   I was so disappointed because the food was great. Not a great birthday treat.

Came to the track on a beautiful Spring day to celebrate friends, with friends, through United Ways 100 Heroes program. The staff, who was clearly marked, is courteous, orderly, and efficient. The grounds were beautiful and one can sense the history just sitting in bleachers.

Coming from NOVA where Salvadoran food spots are a dime a dozen I was so excited that one opened up in South Philly!! I raced to try it. Pupusas are.... a soft spot for me.... 

However ;( mine did not have enough pork and cheese in it resulting in the flavor being a little bland and I had multiple bites of just plain dough. I will however try it again because again.. pupusas are my weakness. Four stars really for just existing in Philadelphia.

Long's! Indianapolis legend. I don't know anyone in Indy who hasn't gone here, prior to them opening (around 4:30-5:00AM), to wait for a fresh warm batch of donuts at least once in their lives. There's a line out the door at the crack of dawn every day for a reason. They can do no wrong in my book!

Party of 14. Toby was our server. Sat outside on the patio and the food was exceptional.  Big party so gratuity was included. Toby wrote on every receipt that gratuity had already been included. No games being played and great service!

Overall nice place, the loft is decent sized.  The lamb burger was fancy no complaints.  The fries are seasoned and crispy.  The crab salad was a little dry but still tasty.  Really no complaints here, the loft has condiments and napkins with decent seating.  Its an upscale market with a huge salad bar and plenty of food to choose from.  The guy at the register brought us a complimentary dessert which was very nice of him.

Mondo is one of my favorite places.  My fiance and I love coming here for date nights.  The service has always been good -- prompt and attentive without being smothering -- and the food is impeccable.  The pate in particular stands out in my memory. 

One of the things I like best about Mondo is the wide variety of daily specials.  These are appetizers, pastas, and pizzas that are always fresh and interesting.  

The prices are very reasonable for the quality of the food.  Another thing I like is that the portions are very reasonably sized.  You can actually order an appetizer, entree, and a side and not waddle home to put on your sweat pants.

The arepas we're by far my favorite thing to get when we came here on a Monday morning right after opening. I packed mine with toppings and two is pretty filling for a meal. These are a must!

If you're looking for a more traditional breakfast, the breakfast croissants next to the arepas are really tasty. I ordered mine packed with bacon, eggs, avocados, and sauces.

This place is worth the trip to the NE and if it was tucked away in a remote corner of Jersey, it would be worth a trip there as well.  The ribs are the absolute best thing on the menu. They fall off the bone and have an amazing smokey flavor. The pulled pork, the brisket, and the half chicken are all amazing in their own way. They have a great daily selection of sides and the pickled accoutrements are delicious. The picnic style tables complete the look and the experience is even more complete since they got their liquor license!

Back today to plan ahead cooking. 
So Italian meatballs, 2 different bags of ravioli and a small lasagna. All can be divided for two meals. And I have room in the freezer. 
Added a fresh baguette and olives from the deli. 
I m set!

Wait was ridiculous for just me & it took 50 minutes ‍. I ordered the bacon cheeseburger with fries & an appetizer pickles.  Burger was over cooked but it did have a good flavor. The bartender that was helping me was very fast with drink refills and bread

When visiting Philly, my sister said, "You have to try this food truck. You just pay this guy $10 and he makes you food. There's no menu, but it's SO good!!" I was totally confused, but intrigued by this. We ended up going two times! This food truck is quite an experience. The man is the only cook and food is made to order. You can watch him cook as you're waiting in line. When I got the food, I was surprised how heavy the box was. It's packed with fresh fruit, veggies, rice, falafel, and chicken covered in this light, creamy sauce. The falafel is homemade. Overall, it's light and heavy at the same time. 

If I visit Philly again, the Octopus Falafel Truck will be a must on my list!
